paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. Sarai had a promise from God and a calendar that wouldn't move, so she came up with her own plan. Abram listened to the voice of Sarai, and the whole house got tangled up in it: Hagar despised her mistress, Sarai blamed Abram, and Hagar ended up running (Genesis 16:2-6). I've seen what happens when I rush a batch because I'm tired of waiting. You get a cookie that looks done and tastes like regret.

But look where the angel of the LORD finds Hagar. She's a servant in the desert with nowhere to go, and he calls her by name (Genesis 16:7-8). Then the angel tells her, "the LORD has heard your cry of affliction" (Genesis 16:11). Nobody in that house was asking how she was doing, and God was listening the whole time. She names Him "the God who sees me," and I'm telling you, I know that feeling from the back of a drawer (Genesis 16:13).

So here's your big idea, baker. When waiting gets long, we reach for shortcuts, and shortcuts can leave people hurting. But God doesn't lose track of anybody, including the ones everyone else overlooked. If you feel unseen today, remember Hagar at that spring. And keep the oven warm, because this story is not over.
